security.title: Regular Expression Denial of Service in jquery-validation
security.description: [CVE-2021-21252](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jxwx-85vp-gvwm): jquery-validation has a regular expression denial-of-service vulnerability. Severity: HIGH. Affected dependency: jQuery.Validation 1.11.1 (declared at WebApp-Storage-DotNet/packages.config:9); affected versions are below 1.19.3. Recommended fix: upgrade to 1.19.3 or later.

The duplicate advisory GHSA-8rfx-6mr3-5jh3 was withdrawn and excluded.

security.title: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
security.description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync takes fileCount directly from the client-controlled Request.Files collection (lines 101-102) and iterates to that count without a maximum (line 106), allowing requests with many file parts to drive unbounded per-file processing.

security.title: Improper Initialization
security.description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.

evidence.explanation: The static blobContainer is only assigned during Index (lines 63-66), but UploadAsync and DeleteImage use it without ensuring Index has run (lines 108 and 135). A direct request to either action before Index initializes the client uses a null resource.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.blobContainer is a mutable static field (line 47). Index assigns it per request (line 65) while UploadAsync, DeleteImage, and DeleteAll read it without synchronization (lines 108, 135, and 158), so requests can access the shared reference concurrently.

security.title: Missing Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

evidence.explanation: The static blobContainer reference is updated by Index and used concurrently by other controller actions without a lock or other synchronization (lines 47, 65, 108, 135, and 158).

security.title: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
security.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.Index creates the blob container with PublicAccessType.Blob (line 66), making uploaded objects anonymously readable. The permission is applied to the gallery's storage container without an access-control check.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: The UploadAsync, DeleteImage, and DeleteAll actions perform security-relevant storage changes (lines 97-174) without recording successful operations or actor/resource details. Exceptions are surfaced to the error view rather than written to an audit or application log (for example, lines 114-118).

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync reads the client-supplied Request.Files[i].FileName (line 101) and passes it directly to BlobClient.UploadAsync as a local file path (line 109). Path elements are not constrained to an upload directory, allowing traversal beyond an intended directory.

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes the untrusted multipart filename from Request.Files[i].FileName (line 101) to BlobClient.UploadAsync (line 109), which treats it as a local path. Relative traversal sequences are not checked or restricted.

security.title: Absolute Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes the client-supplied multipart filename from Request.Files[i].FileName (line 101) directly to BlobClient.UploadAsync as the source path (line 109). An absolute pathname is not constrained to an upload directory.

security.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
security.description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync accepts all multipart files without validating extension or content type (lines 101-110), preserves the submitted extension in GetRandomBlobName (lines 179-182), and stores blobs in a container made publicly readable by Index (line 66). Thus uploaded active content can be publicly served and processed by clients.

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
security.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

evidence.explanation: UploadAsync derives a stored blob name using the user-supplied filename extension (HomeController.cs:108, 179-182), and Index.cshtml places each blob URI into a single-quoted JavaScript argument in an inline onclick attribute (line 53). HTML encoding does not provide JavaScript-string-context encoding; attacker-controlled characters in the retained extension can break out of the string when the gallery is viewed.
